'''Elba Express Pipeline''', also known as the '''SONAT Elba Express III''' and part of the '''Elba III Project''', is an operating gas pipeline in Texas, Georgia, and South Carolina, USA.<ref name=eiajul21>[https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php Natural Gas: Pipelines], US Energy Information Administration, Jul. 27, 2021, accessed Sep. 5, 2021.</ref>

==Location==
The pipeline runs through Georgia, USA and South Carolina, USA.<ref name=fedreg/><ref name=kindermorgan>[https://pipeline2.kindermorgan.com/Documents/EEC/EEC_Segment_Pin_Map-20190625141410.pdf EEC Segment], Kinder Morgan, accessed Sep. 5, 2021.</ref>

==Background==
The pipeline went into service on March 1, 2010.<ref name=eiajul21/><ref name=rigzone/>

It was originally owned by El Paso Corporation<ref name=rigzone/>, which was acquired by Kinder Morgan in 2012.<ref name=businesswire>[https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20120524005835/en/Kinder-Morgan-Inc.-Completes-Acquisition-of-El-Paso-Corporation Kinder Morgan Inc. completes acquisition of El Paso Corporation], Business Wire, May 24, 2012, accessed Sep. 5, 2021.</ref>

It was built in two segments: the Southern Segment and Northern Segment.<ref name=fedreg/> The Southern Segment includes about 104.8 miles of 42-inch pipeline from Port Wentworth to the existing Southern Wrens Compressor Station in Jefferson County, Georgia, USA. The Northern Segment includes about 82.3 miles (10 miles of 42-inch and 75 miles of 36 inch) of pipeline extend from Wrens to interconnections with the [[Transcontinental Gas Pipeline]] in Hart County, Georgia and Anderson County, South Carolina.<ref name=fedreg/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1410838/000095012310028034/h71729exv99w3.htm|title=Pending SLNG/Elba Express Acquisition Exhibit 99.3|last=|first=|date=|website=U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=18 August, 2023}}</ref> U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission authorized the project in conjunction with the Elba III Project which involves the modifications and expansion of storage capacity of the [[Elba Island LNG Terminal]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.energy.gov/sites/prod/files/2016/12/f34/EA-1963%20Elba%20Liquefaction%20FERC%20FEA%20%282016-02%29.pdf|title=Elba Liquefaction Project- Environmental Assessment|last=|first=|date=February 2016|website=U.S. Department of Energy|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=18 August 2023}}</ref>

On 07 June 2016, FERC approved Kinder Morgan's proposal to expand north-to-south capacity on the Elba Express pipeline. Phase 1 of the project which is further divided into three sub-phases,  would add 686.6 Mmcf/day. The first two sub-phases was expected to be operational by November and December 2016 and third by August 2017. Phase 2 and Phase 3 of the project is expected to add 138.1 Mmcf/day and 229.4 Mmcf/day of southward capacity scheduled to be completed by November 2017 and June 2019, respectively.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.argusmedia.com/en/news/1253846-ferc-oks-start-of-elba-express-expansion|title=FERC OKs start of Elba Express expansion {{!}} Argus Media|date=2016-06-07|access-date=2023-08-18|language=en}}</ref> As of August 2023, there has been no update on the expansions.
